messages:
oncall-bot: PAGE: gpu-pool-usw2 - High GPU queue growth detected (>= 4x baseline) | severity: P2 | link: https://redwood.internal/alerts/2498765432

matt: ack — I'm oncall, looking. seeing a big backlog on inference-queue-primary.

sara: I'm pulling metrics now. p50 token latency 120ms -> 400ms last 7m, queue_length = 2.8k (normal ~200).

matt: autoscaler logs show repeated scale attempts failing. grabbing events...

lee: paste of autoscaler events:
```
I0324 14:01:10 autoscaler.go:214] Attempting scale up: desired=60 current=28
E0324 14:01:11 autoscaler.go:317] Scale up failed: API error: quota_exceeded, cannot create more preemptible GPUs in region
E0324 14:01:11 autoscaler.go:318] fallback: no compatible capacity found in spare pools
```

harish: @matt @sara looks like preemptible pool exhausted in us-west2. Spot eviction rate spiked ~14:00 UTC. we're seeing simultaneous preempts.

matt: confirmed — eviction-rate spikes coincide with new ML training jobs in the same region (noisy neighbors).

emily: customer-impact quick check: alpha-corp and beta-app report 429s and increased 500s in the last 10m. support alerted. ETA: unknown.

kevin: trying a manual route change to send critical tenant traffic to dedicated-usw2-burst. running:
```
kubectl patch configmap routing-policies -n redwood --type merge -p '{"data":{"alpha-corp":"dedicated-usw2-burst"}}'
```

ops-bot: deploy-bot: applied routing change to configmap routing-policies (rev 894). Will apply at next config sync.

matt: config sync delay is ~30s. good. also starting manual scale: will request adding on-demand GPUs to fallback pool.

lee: cloud error from GCE on-demand create: "Insufficient capacity in region us-west2 for GPU type A100" — looks like broader shortage.

harish: two-prong mitigation: 1) enable temporary soft-fallback to cross-region pools (us-east1) for non-low-latency tenants; 2) reduce batch size for non-critical routes to throttle queue growth.

matt: implementing plan. rolling routing change: non-critical -> cross-region (us-east1-fallback). patching now.

emily: notif to affected customers: "We are experiencing intermittent capacity constraints in us-west2, we are failover-routing traffic to alternate pools and reducing batch sizes to stabilize latency. We'll post updates every 10m." support posting now.

kevin: manual scale command for fallback pool:
```
redwoodctl capacity add --pool fallback-us-east1 --gpus 8 --type on-demand --reason "incident 2498765432"
```

ops-bot: capacity controller: request accepted, provisioning started (ticket id cap-3421).

matt: monitoring queue: queue_length dropping from 2800 -> 800 after routing changes and batch reduction (5m). p95 latency falling from 1.1s -> 420ms.

sara: tracking autoscaler: we still have failed scaling events due to quota limits; CAP request will take ~12m to provision; need longer term: increase reserved for critical customers.

harish: action items: (1) emergency quota request with cloud team (harish), (2) schedule a Dedicated allocation review for alpha-corp (matt + emily), (3) autoscaler should short-circuit spot-only policy when eviction_rate > 5% (eng runtime/infra task).

matt: handing off to night oncall @lee in 12m. leaving summary: backlog created by region-wide preemptibles exhaustion + autoscaler not failing over fast enough -> temporary cross-region routing + manual on-demand request stabilized service.

lee: ack, I'll monitor for the next 2 hours and follow up with post-incident writeup. adding me to incident channel.

emily: support: ticketed impacted customers and offered failover guidance; assigned account exec for alpha-corp.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigation in place. queue reduced, partial customer failover complete. Next update scheduled in 10m.

matt: closing loop: request follow-up meeting tomorrow to discuss autoscaler rules + reserved capacity for top 5 tenants. tagging @harish @emily @sara.
summary: GPU capacity exhaustion in us-west2 caused by spot/preemptible eviction surge and autoscaler scale-limit errors. Cross-region failover and manual on-demand provisioning used to stabilize queues. Handed off to night oncall.
